Case Study 01

Animazed —
Full-Stack Product Redesign

Product Design Full-Stack UX Research AI Integration Figma Design User Testing

Role

Product Designer & AI/User Researcher

Methods

Moderated Testing

Users

3 Target Participants

Type

E-Commerce Redesign

Overview

The Project

This case study presents a comprehensive full-stack redesign for Animazed Online, an e-commerce platform dedicated to anime, manga, K-pop, and Danmei collectibles. The study aims to assess the entire user journey, emphasizing product design, UX-tailored writing, and UX research. It delivers informed feedback that significantly shapes the final design of the website.

Research

Key Findings

✓ Positive

  • 100% of users could find the FILTER button.
  • 66% found the alphabetized product list helpful.
  • ★ The Pre-Order FAQ page was well-received.
  • 66% found the checkout process efficient.

✕ Negative

  • 100% found the Filter tool required excessive scrolling.
  • ⚠ Filter elements could be better organized.
  • 100% found the Shipping & Return policy page wordy and visually dense.
  • 100% encountered errors navigating back to the homepage via the icon.

User Journey — 3 Moderated Sessions

Insights

Recommendations

Product Navigation & Filtering

  • Reformatted the filter button for better ergonomics.
  • Use drop-down menus for filter options to reduce scrolling and visual clutter.
  • Organize content by fandoms with prominent toggles for "Availability" and "Sales."

UX Writing & Design Revision

  • Reformatted language to appeal to the target audience using familiar phrases via Voice Chart and user testing.
  • Improved visual design aesthetic and organization to enhance overall user experience.
Case Study Breakdown

The Problem

Animazed operates a physical store in Raleigh, North Carolina, and is expanding its online reach. The target users are young adults (18–28) who are active online shoppers for fandom merchandise. The younger generation emphasized a need for a more immersive browsing experience.

The primary goal was to evaluate the end-to-end user journey, focusing on:

  • ◇Effectiveness of product categorization and navigation in facilitating purchases.
  • ◇Usability of specialized navigation tools (filters).
  • ◇Streamlining the purchase journey for high-stress, fast-checkout scenarios.
  • ◇Aesthetic revision of the platform.
Methodology

Research Methodology

3

Target Users

Remote

Moderated Testing

Think

Aloud Protocol

Testing was moderated remotely using the "think-aloud" protocol. Tasks were designed to simulate common user interactions such as product discovery, navigation, and checkout processes. The research focused on identifying user pain points and preferences, providing actionable insights into user behavior.

Process

The Design Process

The iterative design approach was deeply embedded in user feedback at every stage. Midway through the project, an unexpected insight emerged: participants expressed a strong preference for a more immersive visual experience that resonated with their fandom interests — prompting a pivotal shift in design strategy.

"Participants expressed a strong preference for a more immersive visual experience that resonated with their fandom interests."

In response, the site's aesthetics and language were updated to better reflect the target audience's cultural connections, including a dark mode option and fandom-specific language and icons. These adjustments led to:

  • ◇Clearer taxonomy for filters, optimizing product discovery.
  • ◇Reformatted navigation tools and icons to improve the user journey.
  • ◇A consistent visual and linguistic theme that resonated with users.

Design Process — Before & After

Solution

Final Solution

Dropdown Menus

Implemented in product filters to streamline the selection process, allowing users to quickly find preferred items without overwhelming scrolling.

Expandable FAQ

Policy pages reformatted into a digestible FAQ style, enhancing information access and clarity for quick, streamlined navigation.

Themed Consistency

Dark mode, fandom-related language, and icons unified the site aesthetically and linguistically with the target audience's interests.

🔍 ZOOM
✕
Impact

Elevating User Satisfaction & Market Position

The UX redesign focused on making the shopping journey both intuitive and culturally engaging. By aligning the redesign more closely with the audience's preferences through user testing and feedback implementation, the improvements heightened user satisfaction and had the potential to boost conversion rates — underscoring Animazed's dedication to remaining competitive in the e-commerce realm.

Reflection

Adapting Through Continuous Engagement

This project highlighted the critical importance of ongoing user engagement and feedback throughout the design process. Conducting bi-monthly retests ensured that the platform could continuously evolve in response to shifting user expectations and technological trends. The iterative nature of this approach guaranteed that the website stayed relevant, up-to-date, and user-friendly.

Museum Kiosk —
Information Architecture Study

Role

UX Researcher & IA Specialist

Methods

Moderated & Unmoderated

Users

Students Ages 12–18

Context

Women's History Month Pop-Up

Overview

The Project

This research study evaluates the "Echoes of Resistance: A Century of Women's Rights" kiosk design system for a Women's History Month pop-up event. Emphasizing information architecture, user research, AI integration, and key performance indicators (KPIs), the study illustrates how comprehensive methods — including advanced AI analysis — can uncover strategic enhancements for the museum kiosk interface.

These improvements are informed by the target audience's needs, aligned with stakeholder interests, and designed to enhance user engagement and educational impact.

Research

Key Findings

Navigation Efficiency

Simplifying the navigation structure significantly boosted ease of use. AI-driven analytics identified bottlenecks, allowing optimization of pathways effectively.

Engagement & Interactivity

Interactive elements like touch-responsive timelines and quizzes increased user engagement. AI algorithms provided insights into user behavior patterns to maximize interaction.

Content Clarity & Accessibility

AI tools assisted in analyzing text complexity and readability, leading to improved formatting with clear headings — facilitating better understanding of complex historical narratives.

User-Focused IA

Card sorting exercises, enhanced by AI categorization tools, revealed preferred user categorizations — prompting a redesign of the IA to better align with user instincts.

Stakeholder Feedback

Stakeholders appreciated the AI-enhanced analytics' ability to align the kiosk's design with the event's educational goals — exceeding visitor engagement expectations.

KPI Improvements

Key performance indicators like Navigation Ease and Content Comprehension showed marked improvements post-redesign, validated by AI analysis.

Overview

The Project

This case study highlights UX testing conducted for two non-profit organizations — AAA Garcia Bail Bonds and Cats Limited — with the goal to enhance their websites' user experiences. The testing process was tailored to identify usability issues, improve navigation, and streamline access to essential information, increasing engagement and user satisfaction.

Research

Key Findings

AAA Garcia Bail Bonds

Navigation Simplicity

Users found core navigation user-friendly, though the homepage felt cluttered due to an overly fast slideshow.

Social Media Integration

Inconsistencies and non-functional social media links caused user frustration, highlighting the need for standardization.

Information Accessibility

Critical details such as court information were difficult to locate, necessitating better organizational strategies.

Cats Limited

Design Appeal

Positive feedback was received regarding the site's clean design and visibility of contact information, reinforcing the importance of visual appeal.

Link Functionality

Users struggled with identifying and using links — particularly donation CTAs like the Chewy Wishlist — due to a lack of visual cues.

Content Organization

Disorganization and redundant elements led to user confusion and hindered the site's effectiveness in facilitating donations.

🔍 ZOOM
✕
Case Study Breakdown

The Problem

Both organizations faced challenges with site navigation, information accessibility, and content organization, affecting user interactions and overall effectiveness. The websites served different user demographics — AAA Garcia Bail Bonds focusing on legal assistance and Cats Limited on animal adoption and support.

Project Goals

01

Enhancing navigation and accessibility across both platforms.

02

Streamlining information flow and presentation for each unique audience.

03

Ensuring interactive elements like donation and social media links function seamlessly.

🔍 ZOOM
✕
Deep Dive

Research Findings

AAA Garcia Bail Bonds

Navigation & Design

Users found core navigation user-friendly but the homepage felt cluttered due to a rapid slideshow — requiring better pacing to support content absorption.

Surprise: users wanted more vibrant visuals and interactive review summaries.

Social Media Links

Inconsistencies and non-functional links frustrated users.

Surprise: participants also wanted integrated social interaction features directly on-site.

Map & Location

Map compatibility issues were expected.

Surprise: users preferred real-time location updates and interactive directions — a shift toward personalized digital experiences.

Information Organization

Key details were hard to find.

Surprise: users preferred a blog-style feed for real-time updates — a shift toward dynamic content formats.

Cats Limited

Design & Visual Appeal

Clean design was recognized positively.

Surprise: users preferred thematic visuals aligned with adoption stories — a desire for emotional, narrative-driven design.

Link Functionality

Non-intuitive links were a pain point.

Surprise: users suggested a user-generated wishlist integration, emphasizing community interaction.

Content Organization

Redundancy and broken links were expected issues.

Surprise: strong interest in an interactive FAQ feature for dynamic user support rather than static pages.

Impact

Driving Organizational Success

My contribution to these non-profit organizations involved refining their online presence to resonate more deeply with users, ensuring that both AAA Garcia Bail Bonds and Cats Limited can engage effectively with their audiences. These enhancements are expected to increase user satisfaction, improve engagement, and ultimately support the missions of both organizations more effectively.

Reflection

Iterative Design & Human Impact

"Iterative improvements based on thorough user feedback can facilitate better user experiences and drive organizational success."

Working with these non-profits revealed the importance of a targeted UX approach. This project demonstrated the power of aligning site functionality and aesthetics with user needs and expectations — ensuring these platforms remain effective tools for their causes and the communities they serve.

Case Study 04

Second Nature —
CGM AI Companion Dashboard

AI Integration Product Design UX/UI Prototype Claude API

Role

Product Designer & AI Architect

Stack

React · Claude Sonnet

Type

AI-Powered Prototype

Year

2025

Overview

The Project

Second Nature is a personal glucose management prototype featuring Gaia — an AI companion powered by Claude that reads CGM (Continuous Glucose Monitor) data, interprets trends in real time, and generates smart notifications and insulin correction suggestions via a simulated wireless pump system. The project demonstrates how AI can be embedded meaningfully into health-tech UX to create a genuinely supportive and human-centered experience.

The Problem

Designing for Health Anxiety

People managing diabetes face a constant stream of numbers, alerts, and decisions — often without clear context or emotional support. Existing CGM dashboards are clinical and data-dense, leaving users to interpret trends and make correction decisions largely on their own.

The question driving this project: what if your glucose monitor had a voice that actually understood you?

  • ◇Reduce cognitive load around glucose interpretation.
  • ◇Provide emotionally intelligent, AI-driven guidance.
  • ◇Simulate a realistic pump integration for correction boluses.
  • ◇Make the experience feel like a companion, not a device.

Gaia AI Voice

Claude-powered companion that reads your glucose data and responds with warm, contextual insights.

Live CGM Simulator

Real-time glucose chart with trend arrows, time-in-range tracking, and reading history.

Simulated Pump

Basal rate controls, quick bolus delivery, and a delivery log — supporting Omnipod, Tandem, Medtronic and more.

Process

Design Process

01 — Research

Explored existing CGM interfaces (Dexcom, Libre) to identify pain points around alert fatigue, data density, and lack of emotional context.

02 — AI Design

Crafted Gaia's personality through prompt engineering — warm, concise, and medically responsible. Designed the JSON response schema to drive UI decisions.

03 — Prototype

Built a fully functional React prototype with live CGM simulation, Claude API integration, and pump controls — deployable as a single artifact.

"What if your glucose monitor had a voice that actually understood you?"
Live Demo

Interactive Prototype

The prototype below is fully functional. Use Start sim to watch live glucose readings, enter manual readings, and tap Ask Gaia to get real AI-powered insights from Claude. The pump tab lets you manage basal rate and deliver correction boluses.

Second Nature — Gaia CGM Dashboard ⚠ Prototype — not for clinical use
Reflection

AI as a Design Material

"Gaia isn't a chatbot — she's a design decision. Every response she gives is shaped by the UX intent behind her prompt."

This project fundamentally shifted how I think about AI in product design. Rather than treating the API as a backend feature, I approached Gaia's personality and response schema as a core UX deliverable — the same way I would treat a design system or information architecture. The prompt is the design. This prototype demonstrates that AI integration, when handled with intentionality and empathy, can meaningfully reduce user anxiety and elevate a product from functional to genuinely human.
